The Nasdaq 100 staged a 3% recovery following Friday's artificial intelligence rout. Dow Jones futures also surged alongside broader US stock indices.

The Nasdaq 100 staged a 3% recovery following Friday's artificial intelligence rout, driving a broader equity market recovery. Dow Jones futures also surged alongside broader US stock indices. Treasury yields climbed as market participants awaited remarks from New York Fed President Williams.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US stock futures and Treasury yields rebound after AI sell-off

stories.t: US Stock Futures and Tech Shares Rebound Following AI Sell-Off
stories.b: Stock futures are contracts to buy shares at a set price later. Nvidia and Anthropic shares bounced back in premarket trading after a big tech sell-off. The Nasdaq 100 bounced 3% following Friday's artificial intelligence rout. US stock futures and the Dow Jones surged as investors returned to the market.
stories.i: US stock futures climbed in premarket trading as Nvidia and Anthropic shares rebounded from a prior tech sell-off. The Nasdaq 100 staged a 3% recovery following Friday's artificial intelligence rout. Dow Jones futures also surged alongside broader US stock indices.
stories.a: US stock futures advanced following Friday's artificial intelligence sector correction, with Nvidia and Anthropic rebounding in premarket sessions. The Nasdaq 100 recovered 3% as buyers stepped in after the recent valuation fears. Dow Jones futures mirrored the broader index recovery ahead of upcoming Federal Reserve commentary.

stories.t: Treasury Yields Rise and Urban One Faces Nasdaq Notice
stories.b: Treasury yields are the interest the government pays on its loans. Treasury yields jumped as stock futures rebounded and investors awaited a speech from New York Fed President Williams. Urban One is losing its audio co-president and faces a Nasdaq compliance notice.
stories.i: Treasury yields climbed as stock futures recovered and market participants awaited remarks from New York Fed President Williams. Urban One is losing its audio co-president while addressing a Nasdaq compliance notice.
stories.a: Treasury yields jumped alongside equity index futures as investors positioned themselves ahead of New York Fed President Williams' remarks. Urban One reported the departure of its audio co-president while simultaneously processing a Nasdaq non-compliance notification.

politics.b: The Federal Reserve monitors inflation, which is when the cost of living goes up over time. Analysts at TD Securities discussed consecutive rate hikes and sticky inflation.
politics.i: Federal Reserve policy expectations remained under scrutiny as analysts at TD Securities highlighted potential consecutive rate hikes driven by sticky inflation.
politics.a: Federal Reserve monetary policy trajectories faced continued reassessment from analysts at TD Securities, who cited risks of consecutive rate hikes amid persistent inflation pressures.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Pound holds near low, FTSE steady, insurance stress test

stories.t: Sterling Steady After Rebound
stories.b: The British pound is the official money used in the UK. Its value dropped close to the lowest point it has seen in a year. It stabilized because an increase in stock values reduced the strength of the US dollar. Retail sales figures had previously lifted the currency before fading.
stories.i: The British currency held near a 12-month low against the greenback. An equity market rebound trimmed dollar demand and helped the pound firm up. Earlier retail sales gains had already faded amid shifting inflation expectations.
stories.a: Sterling hovered near its 12-month trough as broader equity recovery quelled safe-haven dollar inflows. Fed tightening bets continue to outweigh softer Bank of England rate expectations in driving cross-rate dynamics. The fading impetus from domestic retail sales leaves the exchange rate vulnerable to external US data prints.

stories.t: FTSE Holds Steady Amid Global Rebound
stories.b: The FTSE is a big list that tracks the biggest companies trading on the London stock exchange. The index stayed steady as global indices rebounded following a sell-off in technology shares. Gold prices also jumped while markets recovered from earlier sharp declines.
stories.i: The FTSE index held steady as international equities bounced back from an artificial intelligence sector sell-off. Gold prices recorded gains alongside the broader market stabilisation. Technical selling pressures on major UK indices showed signs of stemming.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 maintained stability as global benchmarks corrected from tech-led liquidations. Precious metal demand surged concurrently, reflecting safe-haven hedging during the broader index recovery. Price action on the London bourse continues to correlate with global risk sentiment shifts.

stories.t: Insurance Regulator Publishes Stress Test
stories.b: The Prudential Regulation Authority is a government group that watches over financial firms to keep the economy safe. This group published the results of a test called the Dynamic General Insurance Stress Test. The test looked at how insurance companies handle tough economic crises.
stories.i: The Prudential Regulation Authority released the findings from the Dynamic General Insurance Stress Test. The exercise assessed the resilience of general insurers against severe simulated market shocks. Regulators emphasised the operational value of rehearsing crisis response mechanisms.
stories.a: The Prudential Regulation Authority finalized its Dynamic General Insurance Stress Test disclosures. Participating institutions modeled complex capital shocks to validate balance sheet robustness. The supervisory output highlights solvency resilience under extreme liability stress scenarios.

politics.b: Government officials watched economic data as retail sales figures shifted and market stress tests concluded.
politics.i: The administration monitored ongoing currency volatility as retail sales momentum faded.
politics.a: State officials evaluated macroeconomic telemetry as sterling approached yearly lows.

0.text: The Prudential Regulation Authority published the 2026 Dynamic General Insurance Stress Test results.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German stocks rebound as ECB expands DLT asset acceptance

stories.t: Frankfurt Stocks Stage Recovery Following Technology Selloff
stories.b: The Frankfurt stock market index, known as the DAX, bounced back after a big drop in technology shares. Bargain hunters stepped in to buy stocks at lower prices. Bayer shares also climbed higher during the trading session.
stories.i: The DAX staged a recovery on probation following a steep technology-led selloff across global equities. European stocks edged higher as buyers returned to the market. Bayer shares outperformed during the session.
stories.a: Equities rebounded from the recent tech-driven liquidation, though technical analysts flag downside risks towards the 24,000 level if ending diagonal patterns hold. The DAX recovery remains fragile as broader market participants assess systemic risk transmission channels.

stories.t: European Central Bank Broadens Collateral Rules for DLT Assets
stories.b: The European Central Bank expanded the types of digital ledger technology assets it accepts as collateral. This allows financial institutions to use more blockchain-based financial instruments when borrowing from the central bank.
stories.i: The European Central Bank widened its acceptance framework for distributed ledger technology assets as eligible Eurosystem collateral. This policy update incorporates modern blockchain tokens into traditional central bank liquidity operations.
stories.a: The Eurosystem expanded operational parameters to include DLT-based assets within eligible collateral pools. This adjustment broadens the institutional acceptance of tokenised collateral instruments for monetary policy counterparty transactions.

politics.b: German exports to Africa are moving toward a record high. At the same time, SoftBank and Nvidia invested in a German robotics company valued at nearly 60 billion yuan.
politics.i: German trade data indicates exports to Africa are heading toward record levels. Concurrently, SoftBank and Nvidia secured major stakes in a German robotics unicorn founded by an entrepreneur from China.
politics.a: Commercial metrics show German exports to Africa tracking toward record volumes. Meanwhile, cross-border venture capital inflows reached nearly 60bn yuan through investments by SoftBank and Nvidia in a domestic robotics enterprise.

timeline: German exports to Africa head toward record highs according to trade data.
SoftBank and Nvidia invest in a German robotics unicorn valued at nearly 60 billion yuan.
European Central Bank expands acceptance of DLT-based assets as eligible collateral.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Yen moves on FX markets and domestic inflation data

stories.t: Yen Rises Against the Dollar as Equities Fall
stories.b: The USD/JPY currency pair fell as an equity rout fuelled demand for the Japanese yen. The dollar slipped from its peaks. Stock market declines drove investors toward safer assets like the yen. The currency pair stalled near 159.00.
stories.i: The USD/JPY pair declined as a broader equity rout stimulated safe-haven demand for the Japanese yen. The dollar retreated from its recent highs near 19-month peaks. Intervention fears capped gains for the currency pair near 160.00. The spot rate hovered around 159 as the stock rally lost steam.
stories.a: Spot USD/JPY compressed as an equity market sell-off triggered a liquidation of risk assets and spurred yen demand. Authorities maintained a implicit ceiling near the 160.00 level, keeping intervention fears active among traders. The currency pair stalled below 159 as broader dollar strength retreated from 19-month highs.

stories.t: Inflation Figures Cool Rate Hike Expectations
stories.b: Modest Japan inflation data cooled bets on a central bank interest rate rise. Central banks change interest rates, which are like the cost of borrowing money, to control price changes. Prices had risen moderately across the country. Traders reduced their bets on tighter monetary policy following the release.
stories.i: Modest Japan inflation readings reduced market expectations for a Bank of Japan rate hike. Consumer price increases came in lower than anticipated by some market participants. Lower price pressures removed immediate urgency for central bank tightening. Traders adjusted their positioning accordingly.
stories.a: Soft domestic inflation prints undermined the policy normalisation narrative and cooled Bank of Japan hike bets. The macroeconomic data printed below consensus, flattening near-term rate expectations. Yield curve pricing shifted to reflect a more patient monetary authority.

politics.b: Data showed the count of people in Japan earning 100 million yen or more doubled over a decade. Japan and Cambodia also planned a stablecoin trial for remittances. Stablecoins are digital tokens pegged to a traditional currency.
politics.i: Official figures indicated the population of earners making 100 million yen or more doubled over a decade. Meanwhile, Japanese and Cambodian authorities planned a yen stablecoin trial to streamline cross-border remittances. Remittances are funds transferred by foreign workers back to their home countries.
politics.a: Demographic income data demonstrated a doubling in the cohort earning 100 million yen or more over a ten-year horizon. Concurrently, Japanese and Cambodian entities advanced plans for a yen stablecoin trial to reduce friction in remittance corridors.

timeline: 23 Nov
USD/JPY slipped near 159.00 as an equity rout drove yen demand.

China.label: China
China.sub: Corporate earnings drops, share buybacks, and bribery sentences

stories.t: Leapmotor Shares Fall Following Profit Drop
stories.b: Shares in Leapmotor dropped 13% in Hong Kong. This happened after the company said its third-quarter profit fell 73%. A share is a tiny piece of ownership in a business. When profits drop, investors often sell their shares.
stories.i: Leapmotor shares dropped 13% in Hong Kong after the electric vehicle maker reported a 73% drop in third-quarter profit. Equity valuations adjusted downward as earnings missed expectations. Lower net income reduces cash flow available for reinvestment.
stories.a: Leapmotor equity fell 13% in Hong Kong following a 73% contraction in third-quarter net income. The 73% earnings compression triggered immediate multiple contraction across the order book. Bears are pricing in lower terminal margins as margin compression outpaces volume growth.

stories.t: Autowell Proposes Share Buyback
stories.b: Autowell controllers Ge Zhiyong and Li Wen proposed a share buyback. They want to buy back up to 120 million yuan of shares. A buyback is when a company purchases its own shares from the market to reduce the total supply.
stories.i: Autowell controllers Ge Zhiyong and Li Wen proposed a share buyback worth up to 120 million yuan. Share repurchases reduce market float and signal internal confidence in the company's valuation. Management teams often deploy this mechanism when equity prices trade below intrinsic estimates.
stories.a: Autowell insiders Ge Zhiyong and Li Wen tabled a proposal to repurchase up to 120 million yuan in equity. The proposed open-market buyback compresses the circulating float. Arbitrageurs evaluate the capital allocation against alternative corporate investments.

stories.t: Former Official Receives Suspended Death Sentence for Bribes
stories.b: Gao Xingfu received a suspended death sentence for taking bribes. He was a former vice-governor of Zhejiang. He took over 100 million yuan in illegal payments. A suspended death sentence is a punishment that can be reduced to life in prison later if the person behaves well.
stories.i: Gao Xingfu received a suspended death sentence for accepting over 100 million yuan in bribes. The court convicted the former Zhejiang vice-governor of corruption. Anticorruption enforcement continues to target high-ranking provincial officials.
stories.a: Former Zhejiang vice-governor Gao Xingfu was handed a suspended death sentence after being convicted of taking over 100 million yuan in bribes. Judicial authorities continue prosecuting elite malfeasance under regulatory governance campaigns. Asset forfeiture accompanies the penal sentencing.

politics.b: The Chinese government continues its strict legal actions against corruption among regional officials. Courts hand out severe punishments to leaders who accept illegal money.
politics.i: Beijing maintains its strict disciplinary oversight across provincial administrations. State prosecutors target senior officials for financial crimes to enforce administrative compliance.
politics.a: Central authorities sustain aggressive prosecutorial sweeps within regional governance structures. State organs utilize severe judicial penalties to deter bureaucratic corruption and enforce political alignment.

timeline: Leapmotor shares dropped 13% in Hong Kong after a profit decline
Autowell controllers proposed a share buyback of up to 120 million yuan

India.label: India
India.sub: Indian equities drop as profit-taking hits major indices

stories.t: Indian Stock Indices Fall Sharply as Profit Booking Accelerates
stories.b: Stock markets are places where people buy and sell tiny pieces of companies. The Sensex and the Nifty 50 are two big collections of India's top companies. Both of these lists dropped sharply by the end of the trading day. Investors sold their shares to lock in previous gains, which is called profit booking. Construction, metal, and bank sectors led the losses during this broad market sell-off.
stories.i: Indian equity benchmarks suffered steep declines as aggressive profit booking drove a broad-based sell-off across multiple sectors. The Nifty 50 dropped 1.75% to close at 25,349, while the Sensex tumbled 1,483 points to settle at 82,435. Construction, metals, and banks acted as the primary laggards in the session. Heavy selling pressure erased recent gains across the broader market.
stories.a: Domestic equity indices experienced a sharp correction driven by institutional profit-taking and systemic long liquidation. The Nifty 50 shed 1.75% to breach the 25,350 threshold, closing down 450 points at 25,349, while the Sensex declined 1,483 points to 82,435. Cyclical sectors, specifically metals, banking, and construction, underperformed significantly due to concentrated unwinding of leveraged positions. The breadth of the decline indicates broad re-allocation rather than idiosyncratic sector shocks.

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Conducts Variable Rate Repo Auctions and State Debt Sales
stories.b: A central bank is the main bank of a country that manages the money supply and interest rates. The Reserve Bank of India held auctions to lend money to commercial banks for short periods. It also managed the sale of state government securities, which are like IOUs issued by regional governments to borrow money from investors. For instance, Assam and Bihar raised funds through these re-issued debt securities at specific yields.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India managed banking system liquidity through multiple short-term operations and state-level debt issuance. The central bank allotted ₹50,005 crore through a four-day variable rate repo auction at a weighted average rate of 5.63%. A separate two-day variable rate repo auction absorbed bids totaling ₹1,37,612 crore, allotting ₹50,003 crore at a weighted average rate of 5.65%. Meanwhile, states including Assam and Bihar raised funds through gilts with varying tenors and yields, such as Bihar's re-issued 2041 securities yielding 8.0932%.
stories.a: Monetary authorities actively managed short-term liquidity distribution via targeted variable rate repo operations alongside sub-sovereign debt absorption. The Reserve Bank of India allotted ₹50,005 crore in a 4-day gilt-backed variable rate repo at a 5.63% weighted average rate against total bids of ₹1,51,982 crore. A concurrent 2-day variable rate repo operation cleared ₹50,003 crore at 5.65%. Concurrently, state-level auctions cleared specific gilt re-issues, with Bihar securing ₹2,000 crore on its 2041 paper at an 8.0932% cut-off yield.

politics.b: Regional state governments in India are borrowing money from financial markets by issuing bonds. The central bank oversees these financial auctions while managing daily money market liquidity. State entities like Assam and Bihar secured funding through these official debt re-issues.
politics.i: Sub-sovereign fiscal management continued through active debt issuance by state governments under Reserve Bank of India supervision. Regional administrations such as Assam and Bihar accessed capital markets to raise specific amounts via dated securities. Concurrently, the central bank utilized short-term liquidity windows to manage interbank funding rates.
politics.a: Sub-sovereign borrowing mechanisms operated via structured state government securities auctions supervised by the apex bank. Regional entities secured targeted capital allocations through re-issued paper across extended tenors while monetary management tools regulated system liquidity through variable rate repo instruments.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras logistics, central bank auction, and corporate deals

stories.t: Petrobras Faces Logistical Hurdles and Schedules Plan
stories.src: CPG Click Oil and Gas · TipRanks
stories.b: Petrobras is a big oil company in Brazil. Operating in the far north region of Foz do Amazonas is very tough. The base is eight hundred kilometres away. The firm invites investors to a webcast for its twenty twenty-seven to twenty thirty-one business plan.
stories.i: Petrobras encounters severe logistical hurdles in Foz do Amazonas due to an eight hundred kilometre distance from its support base. Helicopters, ships, and a lack of ports reveal hidden costs in this isolated northern area. Meanwhile, Petrobras schedules a webcast for its twenty twenty-seven to twenty thirty-one business plan.
stories.a: Petrobras confronts acute infrastructural deficits in Foz do Amazonas, operating eight hundred kilometres from its support base with heavy reliance on maritime and aerial assets. This logistical friction exposes margin erosion from hidden operating expenditures in remote basins. Concurrently, the state-controlled producer prepares its investor webcast outlining capital allocation for the twenty twenty-seven to twenty thirty-one strategic plan.

stories.t: Central Bank Auction and Corporate Acquisitions
stories.b: The Brazilian real fell after a one billion dollar central bank auction. The currency moves towards the six point zero zero to six point three zero zone against the dollar. In corporate news, Banco ABC Brasil buys Angá Asset. Brava Energia finishes a sixty-five percent Pescada acquisition. Companhia Brasileira de Distribuicao spreads one hundred and forty million real of labor debt.
stories.i: The Brazilian real weakens following a one billion dollar central bank auction as the USD/BRL rate targets the six point zero zero to six point three zero corridor. Corporate activity features Banco ABC Brasil agreeing to purchase Angá Asset. Brava Energia finalizes a sixty-five percent acquisition of Pescada. Companhia Brasileira de Distribuicao distributes one hundred and forty million real in labor liabilities.
stories.a: The Brazilian real depreciates post a one billion dollar central bank intervention, driving spot USD/BRL toward the six point zero zero to six point three zero technical band. In domestic M&A, Banco ABC Brasil executes a definitive agreement to acquire Angá Asset. Brava Energia closes its sixty-five percent stake purchase in Pescada, while Companhia Brasileira de Distribuicao restructures one hundred and forty million real of labor obligations across disparate maturities.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: OPEC output decisions and Saudi Aramco contracts

stories.t: OPEC Agreement and Crude Supply
stories.b: OPEC is a big group of countries that sell oil together. They met and agreed on higher oil output for next year. Traders watched these talks closely before oil prices went up.
stories.i: OPEC agreed on higher output for next year. Oil prices rose as traders reacted to the supply decision. The group had previously discussed various production paths.
stories.a: OPEC agreed on higher output for next year, shifting the trajectory for crude benchmarks. Prices responded upward despite competing supply concerns and inflation readings from the United States.

stories.t: Saudi Aramco Expands Partnerships
stories.b: Caturus signed an LNG supply deal with Saudi Aramco. GAS Arabian signed a three-year pipeline installation contract with Saudi Aramco too. Saudi Aramco is a massive oil company in Saudi Arabia.
stories.i: Caturus signed an LNG supply deal with Saudi Aramco. GAS Arabian secured a three-year unit-rate pipeline installation contract with the same firm. Saudi Aramco also stated that oil refining has suffered from underinvestment.
stories.a: Caturus secured an LNG supply deal with Saudi Aramco, matching a three-year unit-rate pipeline installation contract awarded to GAS Arabian. Saudi Aramco executives highlighted broader capital deficits in oil refining infrastructure.

politics.b: Foreign ownership outside of Aramco dropped to 11.01%. Military sources reported ongoing attacks on Aramco by Yemeni Armed Forces.
politics.i: Non-institutional foreign ownership ex-Aramco fell to 11.01%. Military sources stated that Aramco remains under constant attack by Yemeni Armed Forces.
politics.a: Non-institutional foreign ownership excluding Aramco dropped to 11.01%. Operational security remains a factor as military sources report persistent attacks on Aramco infrastructure by Yemeni Armed Forces.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Central bank rate decision and currency pressures

stories.t: Central Bank faces policy dilemma as currency slides
stories.src: Businessamlive · Head Topics · Independent Newspaper Nigeria
stories.b: The Central Bank of Nigeria has a benchmark interest rate of 23%. This is the fee charged on lending between banks, which sets the cost of loans and savings for everyone else. The monetary policy committee is meeting to decide whether to cut, hold, or raise this rate. A cut is difficult because the local currency, the naira, recently dropped by 3%.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Nigeria maintains a benchmark rate of 23% as the monetary policy committee convenes for its final meeting. Policymakers face a inflation and currency pressure dilemma that complicates any ambition to lower borrowing costs. An intervention of $2.5bn failed to ease foreign exchange pressure, leading to a 3% slide in the naira.
stories.a: The monetary policy committee faces a conflicting transmission mechanism as it evaluates the 23% benchmark rate amid persistent inflation and currency depreciation. A $2.5bn foreign exchange intervention failed to halt a 3% slide in the naira, undermining rate-cut ambitions. Policymakers must weigh domestic credit expansion against capital flight risks as official and black market rates diverge.

stories.t: Cardoso supports regional currency plan
stories.b: Olayemi Cardoso backs the single currency project known as ECO for the Economic Community of West African States. This proposed money would exist alongside the current Nigerian currency, the naira. The plan aims to bring together different national economies in the West African region.
stories.i: Olayemi Cardoso backs the ECOWAS single currency initiative called ECO. The proposed monetary unit would circulate alongside the Nigerian naira. The regional integration project is designed to harmonise commerce across West African nations.
stories.a: Olayemi Cardoso endorses the ECOWAS single currency framework, the ECO, to run parallel with the Nigerian naira. The monetary unification strategy seeks to align regional macroeconomic convergence criteria across member states. Implementation timelines remain contingent on member states resolving trade imbalances and foreign exchange disparities.

politics.b: President Tinubu approved 450 billion naira to support local farmers. The government is using state funds to boost agricultural production and assist rural workers. This spending comes as the central bank tries to manage the wider economy and currency values.
politics.i: President Tinubu approved 450 billion naira in agricultural support funding for farmers. The federal intervention aims to boost domestic food production and alleviate supply-side pressures. This fiscal measure runs alongside monetary policy deliberations at the central bank.
politics.a: President Tinubu authorized 450 billion naira in targeted fiscal support for agricultural producers. The spending package seeks to mitigate supply shocks affecting domestic food prices. This fiscal stimulus interacts directly with central bank efforts to manage aggregate demand and curb price growth.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Corporate updates and central bank economic modelling

stories.t: Brambles Issues New Green Bond
stories.b: Brambles issued a new green bond. This is a special type of corporate debt where a company borrows money from investors to fund eco-friendly projects. Brambles uses this funding for circular logistics, which means moving goods in ways that reduce waste and reuse materials.
stories.i: Brambles issued a new green bond to fund sustainable supply chain initiatives. This debt instrument targets environmentally friendly projects within circular logistics frameworks. Investors acquire the fixed-income security to gain exposure to sustainable corporate operations.
stories.a: Brambles priced a green bond specifically earmarked for circular logistics infrastructure. Capital markets participants evaluate the issuance against strict environmental criteria to satisfy ESG mandates. The yield pricing reflects current corporate debt spreads for sustainability-linked instruments.

stories.t: Reserve Bank Model Warns Over Capital Gains Reforms
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of Australia ran economic computer models. The results warn that reforms proposed by Labor could push prices up. This upward push on the cost of everyday goods is called inflation. The modelling suggests specific policy changes might accelerate price growth.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of Australia produced capital gains tax modelling. The central bank analysis warns that Labor's reforms could accelerate inflation. Policymakers evaluate these projections to gauge the broader macroeconomic impact of fiscal adjustments.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of Australia completed econometric modelling regarding capital gains tax structures. The internal forecasts indicate that Labor Party proposals risk exacerbating domestic inflation pressures. Analysts incorporate these findings into monetary policy expectations without observing direct causal certainty.

politics.b: The Reserve Bank of Australia published economic modelling that warns government reforms could increase consumer prices. Political parties face scrutiny over how tax policies affect the wider economy.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of Australia released modelling concerning Labor's capital gains tax reforms. The central bank projections highlight potential risks to price stability, drawing political attention to fiscal policy settings.
politics.a: The Reserve Bank of Australia produced empirical modelling on capital gains tax alterations proposed by the Labor administration. The resulting data injects central bank quantitative warnings directly into the ongoing fiscal debate.

timeline: Brambles issues a new green bond for circular logistics.
Reserve Bank of Australia capital gains tax modelling is released.
